scales.eci_public: Epoch Capabilities Index, public, Bayesian fit of November 2026 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130, GPT-5 = 150). Modelling scale.
scales.aeci_own_card: AECI as printed in the model's own system card. Modelled directly; judgement-heavy. This is what is graded.
scales.aeci_nov6: AECI on the November 6 2026 fit, through a level mapping from public ECI. Secondary.

metadata.interval_convention: median with central 50%, 80% and 95% intervals (lo50/hi50, lo80/hi80, lo95/hi95); null where undefined
caveats: Small samples: 25 Claude models with a public ECI, 21 within-family steps, 8 own-card AECI values, 13 models linking AECI to ECI.
The next-model point forecast is, in effect, 'predecessor + recent record-line slope x elapsed time'. Nothing more elaborate tested better.
Backtest evidence stops at six months ahead (4 folds; 3 with the date unknown, all under-predictions). Haiku's forecast is beyond it.
All backtest folds lie in 2024-26, one regime of rising pace. Every method under-predicted in it.
Beyond about 1.5 years the bands are a scenario projection driven by stated priors, not a validated forecast.
Above the measured-scale threshold (see scale) today's benchmark basket no longer identifies the scale; values there are flagged, not meaningful measurements.
Frontier paths on the 'hold' and faster scenarios carry a pooled under-prediction correction whose out-of-sample test is thin (see projection.bias_term).
Both indices are re-estimated on every update. AECI rests on first-party internal benchmarks; own-card predictions are judgement with a wide band.
Benchmark predictions are anchored on each family's last score; families near a ceiling get a saturation statement instead.
Release dates come from the site's release forecaster; its errors pass straight through.
The model cannot see regime changes it has no data on (new architectures, export controls, a compute shock, a pause).

headline.backtested_through_caveat: 'Backtested through 2027-09-30' means only this: the UNCORRECTED code was run at a 1.0-year horizon from 10 overlapping monthly origins (7 distinct outcomes) in one regime, and under-predicted in 10 of them (mean error +6.3 ECI; 50% coverage 0.40). The corrected configuration that is published has been scored out of sample only at six months, on 12 folds with 6 distinct outcomes.
notes: The next-model point forecasts are, in effect, predecessor + recent Anthropic record slope x elapsed time; in backtest (RMSE 2.5 at release, n=21) they are no better than that two-line rule (RMSE 2.5).

Frontier figures include an under-prediction correction on the 'hold' and faster scenarios only: a pooled 4.7 ECI/yr (sd 4.2; Anthropic-only estimate 6.2, all-lab 4.2), tapered in from zero and out by 1.5 years. It adds 3.2 ECI to those paths at end-2027 (1.8 to the mixture's record-line median). Its out-of-sample check is 12 overlapping six-month folds with 6 distinct outcomes.

Scenario paces in 2027, correction included (ECI points gained by the record line): slowdown 12.1, reversion 15.5, hold 24.0, compounding 34.7, explosive 59.0; mixture 21.3; pre-break pace 15.0, recent pace 20.6.

'Backtested through 2027-09-30' means only this: the UNCORRECTED code was run at a 1.0-year horizon from 10 overlapping monthly origins (7 distinct outcomes) in one regime, and under-predicted in 10 of them (mean error +6.3 ECI; 50% coverage 0.40). The corrected configuration that is published has been scored out of sample only at six months, on 12 folds with 6 distinct outcomes.

The all-lab frontier is the larger of Anthropic's and the other labs'; Anthropic leads in 73% of paths at end-2027 and 62% at end-2030. The other labs' line is fitted on their own records and carries no correction.

Benchmark forecasts are thinly tested (2 to 31 backtest folds per benchmark). Only those marked graded are scored; arena, index and other 'indicative' rows are shown for orientation and are not graded.
The Haiku forecast (median lead about 8 months) lies beyond any tested lead (the longest is six months, 4 folds).
AECI own-card values are judgement-heavy estimates from eight cards (rolling RMSE 3.9).

Above public ECI 196 (80% of today's benchmark basket is already 90% solved at 183, 90% at 196) the basket no longer identifies the scale; rows flagged beyond_measured_scale are extrapolations of the scale itself.
changes_since_previous: Frontier, end-2027 median: 197.5 -> 194.7; end-2030: 251.2 -> 245.9. The under-prediction correction is now pooled across both series (4.7 instead of 5.0 ECI/yr), applied only to 'hold' and faster scenarios, and tapered to zero by 1.5 years instead of being added to every path permanently.
Claude Fable / Mythos 5.3 public ECI median: 179.2 -> 178.4.
'Slowdown' and 'reversion' no longer carry the correction; slowdown now runs below the pre-break pace in 2027. Scenario paces are published as realised gains, correction included.
validated_through renamed backtested_through (2027-09-30; the old key is kept as an alias for this version) and now carries a caveat.

Benchmarks split into graded and indicative. GDPval-AA predictions and the Fable/Mythos Terminal-Bench 2.1 prediction are withdrawn; one saturation rule (latest score or predicted median in the top tenth) replaces per-family inconsistencies. Graded: hle.
All-lab frontier: the non-Anthropic line is now fitted separately and published; the share of paths in which Anthropic leads is reported.
Own-card AECI: gap rule changed to an equal blend of the last gap and the mean of the last three (rolling RMSE 3.9).
Measured-scale threshold is now a range derived from the whole basket (183-196); the page shades from 196 (was 207.6).

scale.range_meaning: public ECI at which 80% / 90% of the 57 benchmarks in Epoch's current basket are at least 90% solved
scale.rule: For each benchmark in Epoch's basket, the ECI at which it is 90% solved is difficulty + 2.2/slope (Epoch's item parameters; all benchmarks, no slope cut-off). The range reported runs from the level where 80% of the basket is that far solved to the level where 90% is; the upper end is the one value the page shades from (the lower end is already close to today's frontier because the basket still holds many old, solved benchmarks). Above the upper end only about one benchmark in ten still separates models, so ECI values are extrapolations of the scale itself. Bands above it are kept in the data and flagged.

trend.note: Record-setting releases since Claude 3 Opus (March 2024). 'hinge' = piecewise linear with unknown changepoint; 'jump' = constant slope with a one-time level shift. BIC weights compare four forms on the published point estimates.

all_lab.series: non-Anthropic records (v2.1; the all-lab frontier is the larger of this line and Anthropic's)
all_lab.note: Fitted to the other labs' records; no step-up is found, so 'pre-break' pace is at most the recent pace and 'reversion' nearly coincides with 'hold' for this series. No under-prediction correction is applied to it. A sizeable share of its slope draws hit the clipping bounds (reported above).

level_process.bootstrap: Subsample bootstrap: each replicate keeps the distinct members of a with-replacement resample of models (about 63%) and one of Epoch's 500 joint posterior draws; record sets are recomputed per replicate. Slope draws outside 4-60 (recent) or 4-40 (pre-break) ECI/yr are clipped to the bound; the share is reported.
level_process.like_for_like: The total slope ratio above (recent / pre-break, public ECI, Anthropic) is the quantity comparable to METR's 1.9x and the card's 1.88x, which are total-slope ratios on AECI. The algorithmic multiplier m used inside the scenarios is a different quantity (it excludes the compute term) and is larger.

gain_model.note: Next = predecessor + max(line gain, 0.3) x exp(c + s z) + measurement noise. The latent step is positive by construction (0 of 21 historical within-family steps were negative); the published score can still fall below the predecessor through measurement noise alone.

families.offsets_note: Offsets from the record line (pooled across families by empirical Bayes) are used only for the family paths after 2027; the next-model forecast uses the gain model. A 'record line + pooled offset' predictor was tested on all folds and is not better (see variants in the release backtest).
families.twin: Fable and Mythos are one underlying model. They are forecast as one entity, 'fable_mythos': one release-date distribution (the forecaster's Fable distribution), one ability draw, one set of benchmark predictions. Public ECI attaches to the Fable label, AECI to the Mythos label.

aeci.primary_scale: Public ECI is the modelling scale (256 models, four years, posterior draws, refittable inputs). AECI is reported two ways: (1) 'own card', the value Anthropic will print in the model's own system card, which is what gets graded and is modelled directly; (2) the November 6 2026 scale, secondary, through a mapping.

summary.rule: equal blend of the last gap and the mean of the last three

own_card.method:
gap_i = own-card AECI_i - public ECI_i (today's Epoch fit; vintage ECI is not available),
one per card that printed an own value, in card order. The gap is a property of the
card's fit (it rose from about -4 to about +4 between May and November 2026, with two
large steps that coincided with basket changes), not of the model's level, so it is
forecast as a level: an equal blend of the last card's gap and the mean of the last
three (v2.0 used the mean of three alone, which scored worse than the last gap in the
rolling test). The predictive sd is the larger of the rolling out-of-sample RMSE of
the blend and the sd of the last four gaps,
widened by sqrt(1 + 0.25 (K-1)) for K card refits before the model's own card. Steps are
not treated as iid and no upward drift is extrapolated. Eight cards: a judgement-heavy
estimate, not a tested forecast.
own_card.label: Judgement-heavy estimate with a wide band. The rolling test (five cards) has RMSE 3.9 AECI points; the Haiku 5.5 card missed by 6.5.
own_card.conditional: Sonnet and Haiku own-card predictions are conditional on Anthropic printing one: the Sonnet 5 card printed no AECI. They expire unresolved if the card has none.

caveats: The gap between AECI and public ECI tracks how recent the model and the fit are, not the model's level: Haiku 5.5 (ECI 160.4) printed 167.11 in its own card. A mapping in level alone under-states Sonnet- and Haiku-tier AECI by roughly 2-4 points; the residual sd is set from leave-one-out and held-out errors to cover that.
The level-shift threshold is not identified between ECI 156.3 and 164.1 (no model in between).
Thirteen models on one fit. Secondary quantity.

refits.note: Descriptive only in v2 (the own-card forecast no longer sums refit steps). Three of the seven card-to-card transitions are observed for Opus 5.5 alone, read from cards that state no fit; over those three refits combined, the other models moved +3.8 to +4.5 and Opus 5.5 +5.4. The two large steps coincide with basket changes, so steps are not exchangeable draws.

links.method: Bounded scores follow p = (score - floor)/(ceiling - floor) = sigmoid(a (ability - D)); the ceiling is estimated (with a bootstrap interval) wherever at least four scores lie above 75% of the nominal range, otherwise the nominal ceiling is kept. Predictions are ANCHORED: the family's own last score, moved along the link by the predicted ability gain (on the logit scale for bounded scores, under a ceiling drawn from its bootstrap and never below the last score), plus step noise estimated from past within-family steps. A benchmark is published only if it is not stale (a model scored in the last six months), not saturated (best score below 90% of the ceiling), not too thin; whether it is graded or only indicative is decided by the admission rule below.

links.admission_rule: A benchmark with a fitted link is dropped if it is stale (no model scored in six months), withdrawn, shows no skill against 'previous in family' on 4 or more folds, or every family is saturated. Otherwise it is GRADED only if it has at least 4 backtest folds, 80% coverage of at least 0.7, |bias| no more than half its RMSE, a resolvable source (a site chart still reporting the family), and an estimated ceiling that does not merely hug the record; every other benchmark is INDICATIVE: shown, not graded. Per family, no number is published if the family's latest score or its predicted median is at or above 90% of the ceiling (a saturation statement is given instead), or if the family's latest model has no score to anchor on.

scale_labels.aeci: Mythos label (Anthropic prints AECI for Mythos)

next_models.note: Each draw takes a release date from the release forecaster, the record-line gain from the shared level paths (scenario mixture, central weights, bias term included), a positive step and measurement noise. Anthropic's Fable 5.2 card prints an unreleased internal model at AECI 178.78 (15 benchmarks); it is not used in the fit.
next_models.monte_carlo: 40000 draws; medians are stable to about 0.05 ECI and interval ends to about 0.2 across seeds.

opus.note: Latest released model in the family. First step is the next-model forecast; later steps follow the record line at the family's pooled offset and cadence.

sonnet.note: Latest released model in the family. First step is the next-model forecast; later steps follow the record line at the family's pooled offset and cadence.

haiku.note: Latest released model in the family. First step is the next-model forecast; later steps follow the record line at the family's pooled offset and cadence.

fable_mythos.note: Latest released model in the family. First step is the next-model forecast; later steps follow the record line at the family's pooled offset and cadence.

scenarios.definition: Below pre-break pace. Training-compute growth follows the 'low' driver path (2.5x, 2x, 1.5x, 1.5x per year 2027-30) and the algorithmic multiplier falls to 0.4-0.9 of its pre-break value within a year.

The 2025-26 step-up was one-off. Pace returns within six months to 0.85-1.15x the pre-break slope (centred on it, so about half these paths run below pre-break pace), then follows the 'central' compute path down.
The recent trend holds: the algorithmic multiplier stays where the recent slope puts it; compute follows the 'central' driver path (5x, 4x, 3x, 2.5x).
AI R&D feedback: the algorithmic multiplier doubles every 6-12 months until it reaches 4-7.5x, then stays; 60-100% of the excess over 'hold' is realised; compute on the 'central' or 'high' path.
Bounded explosive tail: the multiplier doubles every 3-6 months to a peak of 8-30x, holds 1-2 years, then settles at 3-6x; same 60-100% realisation haircut.

projection.weights_are: priors. 'central' is the author's judgement; 'sceptic' and 'accelerationist' bracket it; 'unweighted_evidence_average' is an unweighted average of three unlike data-based numbers, shown for transparency, not an estimate.

evidence_average_detail.warning: Three numbers that span 0.01 to 0.86 are averaged with equal weight; slowdown and explosive are zero only because the sample contains no such episode. Not an estimate.

projection.validated_through_deprecated: alias of backtested_through, kept for one version
projection.backtested_through_caveat: 'Backtested through 2027-09-30' means only this: the UNCORRECTED code was run at a 1.0-year horizon from 10 overlapping monthly origins (7 distinct outcomes) in one regime, and under-predicted in 10 of them (mean error +6.3 ECI; 50% coverage 0.40). The corrected configuration that is published has been scored out of sample only at six months, on 12 folds with 6 distinct outcomes.

layer_agreement.note: Frontier median minus the median implied by the next-model layer's own draws (leader and released next models). Zero by construction until both frontier families have shipped; the frontier is never below it.

projection.validation_statement: 'Backtested through 2027-09-30' means only this: the UNCORRECTED code was run at a 1.0-year horizon from 10 overlapping monthly origins (7 distinct outcomes) in one regime, and under-predicted in 10 of them (mean error +6.3 ECI; 50% coverage 0.40). The corrected configuration that is published has been scored out of sample only at six months, on 12 folds with 6 distinct outcomes. Beyond 2027-09-30 the bands are a scenario projection driven by the stated priors: read each scenario path separately and treat the mixture as a summary of the prior.

calibration_applied.rule: Factors are fitted on the published configuration (pooled correction on trend scenarios). Mixture bands are stretched about the median by the factor for their horizon (interpolated between 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years, held flat beyond). Scenario-conditional bands are not stretched.
calibration_applied.no_op_where: Every factor equal to 1.0 changes nothing: that is all three levels at 0.5 and 1.5 years and the 80%/95% levels wherever raw coverage was already at or above nominal.

bias_term.shape: level adjustment = beta x g(h): g = h^2 up to 0.5 yr, 0.25 + (h-0.5) - (h-0.5)^2/2 up to 1.5 yr, 0.75 after (the correction rate tapers in from zero, peaks at 0.5 yr, and is zero from 1.5 yr)
bias_term.thin_test: A rolling (out-of-sample) correction exists for only 12 Anthropic folds with 6 distinct outcomes, all at [0.5, 1.0] yr. On those it lowered MAE from 5.55 to 4.3; on the all-lab series the same correction changed MAE from 1.77 to 2.21 over 12 folds. Nothing at one year or beyond has been scored with a correction.
bias_term.why_pooled: Trend fits ran low on both frontiers over 2024-26, but block slopes range from -1.0 to 9.2 and the series disagree; a random-effects mean across all blocks is used instead of the Anthropic-only estimate, with the between-block spread carried as its uncertainty.
bias_term.form: level adjustment = beta x g(h): g = h^2 up to 0.5 yr, 0.25 + (h-0.5) - (h-0.5)^2/2 up to 1.5 yr, 0.75 after (the correction rate tapers in from zero, peaks at 0.5 yr, and is zero from 1.5 yr)

reconciliation_with_research_note_1.explanation: Research note 1's central path (17, 17, 16, 15 ECI/yr) is the all-lab frontier continuing at Epoch's reasoning-era slope. For the all-lab series that is our 'hold' and 'reversion' scenarios, which land near it. Our medians are higher for three reasons, in order of size: the Anthropic series has a steeper recent slope than the all-lab series, and Anthropic currently holds the frontier; some prior weight sits on accelerating scenarios; and an explicit under-prediction term is carried where it helped out of sample.

external_comparison.source: AI Futures Project milestones (Automated Coder mid-2028 / mid-2030; SAR 2027 under a held 1.7-1.9x trend)
external_comparison.quantity: Capability milestones from a takeoff model
external_comparison.why: v1 translated ECI into METR-style hours to compare; that translation extrapolated two orders of magnitude beyond METR's measurements and has been withdrawn. The 'compounding' and 'explosive' scenarios are the nearest analogue.

metr_horizon.statement: No hours series is published. METR's last measurement is 17.4 hours (Claude Mythos Preview, April 2026) and METR calls estimates above 16 hours unreliable; the fitted link (about 4.75 ECI points per doubling) has no model above public ECI 157.8. Every released frontier model since then, and every projected value, lies beyond that range, so any hours figure would be extrapolation. Qualitatively: if the link held, each further 5 ECI points would double the horizon.

machine.design: The projection code itself (level.LevelProcess.paths, central scenario weights) run at monthly historical origins and scored on the running-max public ECI 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years later. 'raw' has no correction. 'published_config' is the configuration the live forecast uses: the pooled correction, learned only from folds (of either series) whose target precedes the origin, added on trend-continuation paths. Calibration factors are fitted on 'published_config'. Folds overlap heavily; origins span 2024-07 to 2026-05, one regime of rising pace. The scenario weights are today's prior, so this is not a test of the weights.

correction.shape: level adjustment = beta x g(h): g = h^2 up to 0.5 yr, 0.25 + (h-0.5) - (h-0.5)^2/2 up to 1.5 yr, 0.75 after (the correction rate tapers in from zero, peaks at 0.5 yr, and is zero from 1.5 yr)
correction.thin_test: A rolling (out-of-sample) correction exists for only 12 Anthropic folds with 6 distinct outcomes, all at [0.5, 1.0] yr. On those it lowered MAE from 5.55 to 4.3; on the all-lab series the same correction changed MAE from 1.77 to 2.21 over 12 folds. Nothing at one year or beyond has been scored with a correction.
correction.why_pooled: Trend fits ran low on both frontiers over 2024-26, but block slopes range from -1.0 to 9.2 and the series disagree; a random-effects mean across all blocks is used instead of the Anthropic-only estimate, with the between-block spread carried as its uncertainty.

release.design: Folds are (Claude release, lead) for leads of 0, 3 and 6 months; origin = release date minus lead; everything is refitted on models released strictly before the origin. ALL folds are reported, including the first release of a family (Fable 5), which the model places on the record line. 'model' is told the release date; 'model_date_unknown' is given only the family's cadence up to the origin and is the relevant test of the live forecasts at leads above zero. A baseline is scored on every fold where it is defined (n is shown per row).
release.verdict: On all folds the model's point forecast is not distinguishable from 'previous-in-family + trailing-12-month Anthropic record slope x elapsed time' at any lead (every paired interval spans zero, or favours the baseline). That baseline is therefore the core of the model: next = predecessor + recent record-line gain. What the model adds is a predictive distribution with tested coverage, a positive-step constraint, and consistency with the long-range paths. It does clearly beat 'previous model in family', 'family mean step' and the two all-lab trend lines.
release.what_n_supports: Lead 0 (n=21) supports an error of roughly 2.5 ECI points RMSE with the date known. Three months ahead (n=10, 9 with the date unknown) supports 'about the same, perhaps 3'. Six months ahead (n=4, 3 date-unknown) supports nothing firmer than 'errors of 4-6 points happened and every one was an under-prediction'. No fold has a lead beyond six months: the Haiku forecast (median lead about eight months) is outside anything tested.

calibration.rule: Per level, the larger of the two sets' factors; never below 1.

irt_refit_check.design: Own least-squares 2PL refit of Epoch's benchmark-level inputs, refitted at every fold origin on models released on or before that date, mapped to ECI units by a monotone alignment to the published ECI of those same models. The release backtest is rerun with history from a strict-origin vintage (models released before the origin; in v2.0 the lead-0 vintage included the target) and the target's actual from the release date's vintage. The fit is deterministic; the vintages are stored in data/irt_vintages.csv.gz, which is committed and covered by the input hash (run.py --full rebuilds it; a test recomputes two vintages and compares).
irt_refit_check.v1_bug: In v1 a date-rounding slip excluded the target from its own vintage on a clean cache, which is why the reviewer's clean run found 18 folds instead of 33. Fixed (tolerance on 'on or before'); numbers below are from a clean rebuild.
irt_refit_check.caveat: Scores in Epoch's input file are today's collection; a score measured after the origin for a model released before it cannot be removed (no timestamps).

benchmarks.design: Same folds as the release backtest (families with an earlier score on the benchmark). 'anchored' is the published method; 'curve_level' is v1's method (the fitted curve's level at the predicted ability), kept for comparison; baseline: the previous model in the family.

review.title: Headline backtest omitted the worst fold; strawman baselines
review.action: Every table is on all folds (Fable 5 included; a first-of-family release is placed on the record line). The reviewer's baseline is a named baseline with paired differences and bootstrap intervals. 'Beats every baseline' is withdrawn: the model is not distinguishable from previous-in-family + trailing-12-month slope, which is now its core.

review.title: Benchmark predictions contradicted observed scores
review.action: Ceilings are estimated where the data allow; predictions are anchored on the family's own last score; saturated, stale and thin benchmarks are dropped with reasons; a family already within a tenth of the ceiling gets a saturation statement instead of a number; tests check every open prediction against observed scores.

review.title: Corner-solution stacking; the two layers disagreed
review.action: Stacking is gone. One level process (equal weights over three recent-trend forms; no all-history forms) feeds both the next-model layer and the projection from the same simulated paths.

review.title: The 2027-30 band was an untested prior
review.action: The projection code is now backtested at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 years on both frontiers, its bias term is estimated out of sample and carried with uncertainty, and its calibration factors are applied. The all-lab frontier is fitted to all-lab data. A below-pre-break scenario exists. Beyond 1.5 years nothing can be tested: those bands remain a prior and are labelled as such; values above the measured scale are flagged.

review.title: Implied METR horizon was false precision
review.action: The hours series and the work-month / work-year probabilities are removed; a qualitative statement replaces them.

review.title: AECI layer
review.action: Own-card AECI is modelled directly from the eight own-card values and labelled a judgement-heavy estimate; refit steps are no longer summed as iid draws; Sonnet/Haiku predictions are marked conditional. It is still eight cards: the rolling test is poor and is reported.

review.title: Twins and grading
review.action: Fable and Mythos are one entity. Unresolvable predictions are pruned; grade.py has an expiry rule and grades against the first published value.

review.title: Regression odds contradicted the record
review.action: Positive-step model; implied P(regression) is reported per entity and is a few percent, from measurement noise only.

review.title: Section 7.4 not reproducible
review.action: Root cause was a date-rounding bug that dropped the target from its own vintage on a clean cache. Fixed; vintages are committed, hashed and tested.

review.title: Live leads untested; calibration a no-op
review.action: The date-unknown variant is the headline for leads above zero and the limits of n are stated. Ability calibration factors are still 1: raw coverage on all folds is at or above nominal, so there is nothing to widen. That is a finding, not an omission; the frontier bands do get non-trivial factors. Haiku's eight-month lead remains untested and is flagged in the output.

review.title: Name-matcher merges
review.action: Dated variants no longer merge into siblings; explicit aliases for Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Oct/Jun); every non-exact match is logged.

review.title: Bootstrap was a subsample; slope draws truncated
review.action: Called a subsample bootstrap; draws are clipped (not discarded) and the clipped share is reported.

review.title: Tests asserted what the code wrote
review.action: Leak tests perturb future data and require unchanged predictions; the mapping test is leave-one-out.

review.title: Monte Carlo noise comparable to differences
review.action: Draws raised; a second-seed rerun is reported; candidate differences inside that noise are no longer interpreted.

review.title: m compared with METR's total-slope ratio
review.action: The total slope ratio is reported for the like-for-like comparison.

review.title: Degenerate frontier floor
review.action: The standing leader's value is drawn from Epoch's posterior.

review.title: Full-sample tuning choices (df, floors, half-life)
review.action: Left as stated assumptions (METHODS section 11). The reviewer measured their effect at RMSE 2.36-2.83, inside fold noise; tuning them by nested cross-validation on ~20 folds would add machinery without changing any number that matters.

review_second.title: Bias term added to every scenario and hidden from the scenario table
review_second.action: The correction is pooled across both series by random effects, applied only to 'hold' and faster scenarios on the Anthropic line, tapered in from zero and out by 1.5 years. Scenario paces are published as realised gains with the correction included; 'slowdown' runs below the pre-break pace in 2027.

review_second.title: 'The correction helped' rested on four folds
review_second.action: The thinness of the test is stated wherever the correction is mentioned (METHODS 7.2, headline.notes, projection.bias_term). The pooled estimate replaces the Anthropic-only one. It remains a correction estimated in one regime and untested beyond six months.

review_second.title: 'Validated through' too strong
review_second.action: Renamed backtested_through (alias kept one version), derived without the 0.13-year allowance, with a caveat attached.

review_second.title: GDPval-AA over-extrapolates
review_second.action: Withdrawn. No concave link was fitted: with 12 folds and a board that re-anchors, there is nothing to validate one against.

review_second.title: All-lab frontier was mostly Anthropic's and inherited its correction
review_second.action: The non-Anthropic frontier is fitted on its own records, carries no correction and is published; the all-lab frontier is the larger of the two; the share of paths in which Anthropic leads is reported per year-end.

review_second.title: Fable/Mythos Terminal-Bench 2.1 anchored on Fable 5.1
review_second.action: A prediction now needs a score from the family's latest model; this one is withdrawn.

review_second.title: Admission rule text disagreed with code; inconsistent saturation
review_second.action: One rule in code and text: graded needs 4+ folds, 80% coverage >= 0.7, |bias| <= RMSE/2, a resolvable source and a ceiling that does not hug the record; everything else with a link is indicative. A family gets no number if its latest score or predicted median is in the top tenth.

review_second.title: Layers agreed to ~1 ECI, not Monte Carlo noise
review_second.action: The frontier is built from the next-model layer's own draws until both frontier families have shipped; projection.layer_agreement reports the shortfall per quarter and a test bounds it.

review_second.title: Lead-0 vintage included the target
review_second.action: History now comes from a strict-origin vintage.

review_second.title: Grading matched chart rows by exact date
Measured-scale threshold lenient
review_second.action: Reported as a range from the whole basket; the page shades from its upper end.

review_second.title: Calibration factors fitted on a different configuration
review_second.action: Fitted on the published configuration; METHODS says where they are a no-op.

review_second.title: Own-card rule scored worse than 'last gap'
review_second.action: Equal blend of the two rules.

review_second.title: Claude 3.5 Haiku entered vintages 13 days early
All-lab slope draws clipped 19.8%
review_second.action: Reported in trend.level_process; the other labs' record series is short and noisy and the clipping bounds are wide (4-60 ECI/yr).
